newsitem.title: USA: Money managers mixed on U.S. debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers mixed on U.S. debt -- survey.

text.p: Money managers' activity was mixed in U.S. debt markets last week, leaving little net change in portfolios, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"The nature of the flows (last) week were less one-sided," the report said.

"Money managers have become much more defensive following Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, and had reduced duration exposure and raised some cash in each of the prior two weeks," it said.
In the week ended March 18, duration bogey fell to 4.14 from 4.16 on an arithmetic basis and rose slightly to 4.70 from 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.76 from 4.88 on an arithmetic basis. It dropped to 4.98 from 5.01 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio declined to 7.18 percent from 7.64 percent.
Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 16 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active rose to 5.33 from 4.25 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
